t: Sangam-age Tamilakam was the ancient Tamil-speaking country of southern India, divided among the Chera, Chola and Pandya kings and lesser chieftains, the Velir.
Its 2,381 surviving poems by 473 poets, at least 27 of them women, sing of love and war and are the earliest known literature of South India.
Farming, weaving, pearl fishing and shipbuilding supported a sea trade in pearls, pepper and textiles that brought Roman coins to Kerala and Tamil Nadu.
dyk: The Sangam poems were forgotten for much of the second millennium; in 1883 U. V. Swaminatha Aiyar found a major store of their palm-leaf manuscripts in the library of the Thiruvavaduthurai Adhinam, a Shaiva monastery.
ev: A settlement at Keezhadi, near Madurai, is occupied, according to radiocarbon dating
Inscriptions of the time of the Maurya Empire give the earliest datable references to the Tamil kingdoms
Two adventurers from southern India take control of the Anuradhapura kingdom in Sri Lanka
Elara, a Chola general or prince, takes the throne of Anuradhapura and rules for forty-four years
The span Kamil Zvelebil finds most acceptable for the Sangam poems
The Periplus of the Erythraean Sea describes Muziris, a Chera port of the trade with Rome
U. V. Swaminatha Aiyar finds major Sangam manuscripts at the Thiruvavaduthurai Adhinam
A survey along the Vaigai river led by Amarnath Ramakrishna identifies Keezhadi among 293 sites with archaeological remains

f.homeland: Tamilakam, “home of Tamil”: today’s Tamil Nadu, Kerala, Puducherry, Lakshadweep and southern Andhra Pradesh and Karnataka; cities Madurai, Uraiyur, Kanchi and Puhar; ports Korkai and Muziris; the excavated site of Keezhadi
f.period: Usually c. 300 BCE–300 CE; Kamil Zvelebil finds 100 BCE–250 CE most acceptable for the poems; some accounts begin the age c. 600 BCE, and Keezhadi is radiocarbon-dated to the 6th century BCE; post-Sangam literature c. 250–600 CE
f.known: Sangam poetry of love (akam) and war (puram); the Tolkappiyam grammar; the three crowned dynasties, Chera, Chola and Pandya; the Velir chieftains; pearls, pepper and textiles; sea trade with Rome
f.sources: 2,381 Sangam poems by 473 poets; Tamil-Brahmi and other inscriptions, including Ashoka’s and Kharavela’s; Greek and Roman writers (the Periplus, Pliny, Ptolemy); Roman coins and amphorae; excavations such as Keezhadi
